executive_summary: The 47th Dutch parliamentary session on March 4, 2026, focused primarily on the Selibon waste management crisis in Bonaire, where serious environmental and health violations have persisted despite years of intervention attempts. Parliament achieved broad cross-party consensus on urgent action, approving multiple motions for RIVM air quality monitoring, implementation of Ombudsman recommendations, and regional waste cooperation, while the government sought additional time for coordinating relocation plans and budget allocations. Additional discussion covered island council expansion and portfolio transitions between ministries.

main_topics.topic: Selibon Waste Management Crisis in Bonaire
main_topics.summary: Extensive debate on environmental and public health hazards at the Selibon waste facility, including illegal dumping, air quality violations, recurring fires, and health risks to residents. Parliament expressed frustration with years of stagnation and insufficient government intervention, with all parties calling for immediate, coordinated action involving RIVM monitoring, resident relocation, and structural solutions.

party_positions.ChristenUnie (Ceder): Supports urgent intervention with RIVM monitoring, relocation plans for affected residents, and implementation of National Ombudsman recommendations. Expressed hope that new government officials will finally resolve this 'great injustice'.
party_positions.GroenLinks-PvdA (Tseggai): Emphasizes urgent solutions and government coordination; advocates for RIVM monitoring, Spring Budget funding, and regional cooperation between Bonaire, Aruba, and Curaçao on waste management.
party_positions.Groep Markuszower (Schilder): Advocates for direct state control of permitting, oversight, and enforcement, arguing that lighter interventions are irresponsible given years of stagnation and public health/environmental risks.
party_positions.CDA (Van den Brink): Supports expansion of island councils and rapid legislative treatment to meet 2027 election timeline; concerned about prior coalition agreements on statutory language.

main_topics.outcome: Parliament approved 7 motions: RIVM continuous air quality monitoring (Motion 442), National Ombudsman recommendations implementation (Motion 444), regional waste cooperation exploration (Motion 446), and direct state control integration (Motion 447). Government received until summer for relocation plan coordination (Motion 443, marked Ontijdig). Spring Budget funding request (Motion 445) marked Ontijdig due to procedural constraints. Government adopted advance planning motion (Motion 448).

main_topics.summary: Discussion of expanding island councils before the 2027 elections, with concerns about budget sufficiency and proper implementation. Parliament questioned whether adequate resources have been inventoried for the expansion.

party_positions.CDA (Van den Brink): Seeks rapid legislative treatment to meet 2027 election deadline, requesting confirmation of political commitment.
party_positions.GroenLinks-PvdA (Tseggai): Not opposed to expansion but previously sought clarification on timeline necessity; supports due diligence on budget adequacy.

main_topics.outcome: New Motion 50 introduced for voting to inventory actual funding needed for island council expansion before final legislative reading. State Secretary to consult with island councils before finalizing legislation and report back to Parliament in writing.

main_topics.summary: Clarification discussions regarding the transition of the Selibon circular economy portfolio between the Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management (IenW) and the new Climate and Green Growth ministry.

party_positions.State Secretary Bertram: Confirmed that circular economy portfolio is transferring ministries but emphasized careful coordination between both state secretaries to ensure continuity of responsibility and prevent gaps in oversight.

main_topics.outcome: Both state secretaries coordinating during the transition; Parliament satisfied with assurances that responsibility will not fall through administrative cracks.

key_decisions: Motion 442: Government agrees to establish continuous air quality monitoring by RIVM at Selibon Lagun (Approved)
Motion 443: Temporary relocation plan for affected residents (Marked Ontijdig - government granted until summer for multi-ministry coordination)
Motion 444: Government to implement National Ombudsman recommendations on illegal dumping intervention (Approved)
Motion 445: Funding proposals in Spring Budget for structural Selibon solution (Marked Ontijdig due to budget process requirements)
Motion 446: Government to explore collaboration with Aruba and Curaçao on joint waste management (Approved)
Motion 447: Direct state control integration of permits/oversight into overall intervention process (Approved)
Motion 448: Government to develop concrete plans for immediate action once procedurally possible (Adopted by government)
Motion 50: Parliament to inventory actual funding needed for island council expansion before final legislative reading (Introduced for voting)
State Secretary to consult with island councils before finalizing legislation approach and report back to Parliament in writing
political_dynamics: Parliament demonstrated rare unified cross-party consensus on the urgency of the Selibon crisis, with positions ranging from ChristenUnie and GroenLinks-PvdA seeking coordinated intervention through normal channels to Groep Markuszower advocating for more aggressive direct state control. The government appeared receptive to most motions but invoked procedural constraints (marking certain motions 'Ontijdig') to avoid pre-committing to Spring Budget allocations. Minor tensions emerged around coalition governance (Tseggai questioning CDA participation in controversial statutory language negotiations) and speaker time allocations for smaller groups. Overall, the session reflected a functioning parliamentary system balancing urgency with procedural integrity, with the government maintaining flexibility while Parliament pushed for concrete timelines.
next_steps: RIVM to establish continuous air quality monitoring at Selibon Lagun facility
Government to coordinate across three ministries and with public authority on temporary relocation plan for affected residents (deadline: summer 2026)
Government to implement National Ombudsman recommendations regarding illegal dumping intervention
Government to explore and report on regional waste management collaboration opportunities with Aruba and Curaçao
Government to develop concrete action plans for immediate implementation once procedurally possible

State Secretary to submit written report to Parliament on island council consultations before law treatment
Parliament to vote on Motion 50 regarding island council expansion budget inventory
